name: ATV (quad bike)
description: A four-wheeled quad bike: ATVs, farm quads and sport quads. The rider sits astride it and steers by the handlebars, all four wheels pull, and it is light, narrow and nimble off the road.
comment: A vehicle preset (#728); see sedan.json for the format. The real machine is a Polaris Sportsman 570 (#376 step 9d), from Polaris's published specs: 567 cc ProStar single, 44 hp, an automatic PVT (a CVT) with on-demand AWD, 318 kg (701 lb) estimated dry weight plus about 12 kg of fuel, 128.3 cm (50.5 in) wheelbase, 210.8 x 121.9 x 119.4 cm, 29.2 cm ground clearance, an 84.5 cm seat, 25 x 8-12 front and 25 x 10-12 rear tires (31.75 cm radius) and 20.8 / 24.1 cm of travel. No instrumented test was found, so it is reported, not judged. Its rider straddles it on a motorcycle seat (chassis.rider): a quad's, whose four wheels steer themselves and whose grips ride a handlebar bone between them (#376 step 9d). ABS and traction control are off (real quads have neither; Joshua 2026-11-25), and both axles drive all the time. Its belt drive (transmission.cvt, ATV follow-on) is a real CVT: the engine holds 6500 rpm at full throttle while the belt slides from 3.1 to 0.75, then the EBS high-range box, 11.12:1 in Polaris's manual (x 32 / 31.75 for our wheel = 11.21, split as gear 1.2 x final drive 9.34 to stay under the 10 limit), and reverse 21.74 / 11.12 x 1.2 = 2.346. Its low range (transmission.lowRange, G or Back + D-pad Up) is the EBS low box over the high one, 23.91 / 11.12 = 2.15. chassis.hitch (#446) is a tow ball 10 cm behind the body's rear end, as on the pickup and van, but 35 cm up, a quad's rear receiver height, for the utility trailer (utilitytrailer.json). The low ratio is worked out from Polaris's ~3,000 rpm at 3 mph in low range (generic Polaris manual), the high one from the ~93 km/h the blogs give at the shift rpm. Estimates: the torque (52 Nm at 5500 rpm, 48 at the 6500 rpm power peak, which the belt holds), the 7000 rpm limit, the ~90 km/h top speed (the governor), the 97 cm track, the 45/55 split, the drag and frontal area, the 110 cm body, the handlebar, footboards and seat, and a 0.65 g grip on asphalt (knobby tires): friction 0.9 (1.0 cornered at 0.725 g). The centre of mass sits at the car type's stability bound (42 cm; a real quad's is nearer 50, so this one tips less easily). Springs, damping, brakes and engine braking follow steps 7-9's rules, with springs for a 1.8 Hz ride with a rider on board. Its tire forces act at the wheel centres, not the contact patch as a car's do: at the patch the light, narrow quad rocked side to side at rest.
